channel.title: Intellexa Journal
channel.description: Independent local reporting: world, U.S., business, finance, politics, health, technology and investigations.

item.title: The Vanity That Led To the Downfall of Alina Habba Mildon
item.description: Beauty, Power, Ambition and the Price of Loyalty: From the White House to the Herrera Velutini Banking Dynasty

item.title: US Diesel Prices Climb to Record $5.85 a Gallon, Straining Transportation and Consumer Budgets
item.description: Diesel prices across the United States climbed to an all-time high this week, a jump tied to the ongoing conflict with Iran that is already rippling through freight, groceries and household budgets.

item.title: August Payrolls Surge Past Forecasts, Keeping Fed Rate Hike Alive
item.description: A surprisingly strong August employment report has revived expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month, even as underlying signals in the labor market remain mixed.

item.title: Stocks Slide as Strong Jobs Report Raises Odds of a Fed Rate Hike
item.description: A surprisingly strong August jobs report sent all three major U.S. stock indexes lower Friday, as traders bet the data gives the Federal Reserve more room to raise interest rates.

item.title: Control of the House Hangs in the Balance as 2026 Midterm Season Reaches Its Final Stretch
item.description: With all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats on the ballot this November, both parties are pouring record money into a small number of true battlegrounds that will decide who runs Washington.

item.title: US Measles Cases Hit a 30-Year High as Vaccination Gaps Widen in Several States
item.description: Two children have died in the current outbreak season as public health officials warn that falling vaccination rates are eroding decades of progress against the disease.

item.title: More Large Employers Are Dropping Health Coverage as Insurance Costs Keep Climbing
item.description: Rising premiums are pushing some companies to scale back benefits or shift more costs onto workers, raising fresh concerns about employer-based health coverage in the United States.

item.title: CDC Advisory Panel Recommends Second RSV Vaccine Dose for Some Children
item.description: The updated guidance reflects a growing consensus that a booster dose can provide meaningful additional protection against a virus that remains a leading cause of infant hospitalization.

item.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-6 Astra and Declares the Start of the AGI Era
item.description: The new frontier model brings sweeping gains in reasoning and cyber capability, and it has already been rated a critical risk under OpenAI's own safety framework.

item.title: Tesla's Wheel-Free Cybercab Hits Austin Streets and Immediately Draws a Federal Safety Probe
item.description: The driverless robotaxi rollout marks a major step in Tesla's autonomy push, but early incidents have prompted regulators to open an investigation within days of launch.

item.title: AI Infrastructure Startup Crusoe Vaults to a $30 Billion Valuation
item.description: The rapid rise of the data center developer reflects investor appetite for companies building the physical infrastructure underpinning the AI boom.

item.title: Investigation: Dark Money Groups Are Pouring Record Sums Into the 2026 Midterms — And Voters Often Can't Trace It
item.description: An Intellexa Journal review of campaign finance filings found a growing share of political spending this cycle is coming from groups that are not required to disclose their donors.

item.title: Justice Department Faces Mounting Pressure Over Review of Epstein Case Documents
item.description: Officials are working through more than five million pages of records as lawmakers from both parties demand greater transparency about what investigators knew and when.

item.title: FDA Approves New Drug for Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer, Offering New Hope for Patients
item.description: The approval of daraxonrasib gives oncologists a new treatment option for one of the deadliest and hardest-to-treat forms of cancer.

item.title: Investigation: How Thousands of US Nursing Homes Keep Failing Minimum Staffing Rules — With Few Consequences
item.description: An Intellexa Journal review of federal inspection records found a pattern of repeated staffing violations at nursing homes across the country, with penalties that rarely change underlying behavior.

item.title: Investigation: AI Data Centers Are Straining Local Water Supplies in Drought-Prone Communities
item.description: As tech companies race to build the infrastructure powering the AI boom, an Intellexa Journal review found several facilities are drawing significant water for cooling in areas already facing scarcity concerns.

item.title: Ed Markey Turns Back Primary Challenge From Seth Moulton in Massachusetts Senate Race
item.description: The 80-year-old incumbent defeated a House colleague who argued Democrats needed younger leadership, an early test of the party's generational divide heading into November.

item.title: US Forces Strike Three More Alleged Drug Boats as Caribbean Campaign Escalates
item.description: The latest strikes bring the total number of vessels targeted this year to dozens, part of a hardline campaign the administration says is aimed at cartel trafficking networks.

item.title: Cyclosporiasis Outbreak Raises Alarm Over Cuts to Food Safety Inspections
item.description: Public health investigators say the parasitic outbreak, linked to fresh produce, has been harder to trace after reductions in federal and state food inspection staffing.

item.title: Large Study Finds Hormone Therapy Linked to Lower Dementia Risk in Women
item.description: Researchers say the findings could reshape how doctors and patients weigh the benefits and risks of hormone replacement therapy during and after menopause.
